Theorem
[Lower bound for the heat kernel] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0381, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0382 ↗ lem:chow-iii-evolving-heat-kernel-diagonal-lower-bound 1. ch26:26.31\group Heat Kernel Lower Bounds

There are $c_1,c_2>0$, with the curvature dependence specified in the source, such that \[ H(x,\tau ;y,v)\ge c_1 \min \left\{ \frac1{\Vol _{\widetilde g}B_{\widetilde g}(x,\sqrt{\tau -v})}, \frac1{\Vol _{\widetilde g}B_{\widetilde g}(y,\sqrt{\tau -v})} \right\} e^{-d_{\widetilde g}(x,y)^2/(c_2(\tau -v))}. \] Equivalently, after changing constants, one may use the geometric mean of the two reciprocal volumes.
Proof

\sketch Apply the Li–Yau Harnack inequality between $(x,\tau )$ and the diagonal point ($y,(\tau +v)/2$), then insert the diagonal lower bound. Repeat with (x,y) interchanged and combine the two estimates.

□
